_notice: DEMO DATA. Every item below is invented to design the interface. None is a real article, and no value is a real measurement. Replace MockNewsProvider with a real provider to remove this file.

items.headline: Sample: large energy conglomerate announces new refining capacity plan
items.why: Capacity announcements change expected volumes and capital spending for the largest index weight.
items.explanation: Demo explanation: a capacity plan of this kind would normally be read against funding cost and expected margins. In a real module this text would summarise the timestamped article.

items.headline: Sample: central bank keeps policy rate unchanged, signals data-dependent stance
items.why: Rate decisions move bank margins, bond yields and the discount rate for every sector.
items.explanation: Demo explanation: an unchanged rate with a data-dependent stance is usually close to consensus. A real module would compare the decision with the pre-announcement expectation.

items.headline: Sample: IT services major trims full-year revenue guidance
items.why: Guidance cuts from one large exporter are often read across to the whole sector.
items.explanation: Demo explanation: the read-across to peers is the interesting part of this event type. A real module would measure the peer reaction separately from the company reaction.

items.headline: Sample: monthly consumer inflation prints below expectations
items.why: Lower inflation raises the chance of easier policy and supports consumer demand.
items.explanation: Demo explanation: the surprise relative to expectations matters more than the level. A real module needs the consensus figure with a timestamp before the release.

items.headline: Sample: crude oil rises after supply disruption headlines
items.why: India imports most of its crude, so higher prices weigh on the currency and on fuel users.
items.explanation: Demo explanation: the effect differs by sector: refiners and producers can gain while fuel users lose. A real module would show each separately.

items.headline: Sample: benchmark index closes higher for a third session on broad buying
items.why: A market-wrap item: it describes what happened and rarely carries new information.
items.explanation: Demo explanation: wrap-up stories are published after the move, so they score low on novelty. A real module would flag them as non-novel.

items.headline: Sample: government announces infrastructure spending package
items.why: Public capital spending feeds order books for construction, cement and capital goods companies.
items.explanation: Demo explanation: the size relative to the existing budget and the timing of actual spending decide the effect. A real module would link the official announcement.

items.headline: Sample: private bank reports stronger quarterly loan growth
items.why: Loan growth is the main volume driver of bank earnings.
items.explanation: Demo explanation: business updates before results often move the stock more than the results. A real module would tag this as a pre-earnings update.

items.headline: Sample: US central bank officials signal slower pace of rate cuts
items.why: US rates drive foreign flows into emerging markets and the dollar earnings of exporters.
items.explanation: Demo explanation: overnight global events reach the Indian market at the next open, which is why timestamps matter for any event study.

items.headline: Sample: market regulator proposes tighter rules for derivatives trading
items.why: Derivative rule changes affect exchange and broker volumes and intraday liquidity.
items.explanation: Demo explanation: a proposal is not a final rule. A real module would separate consultation papers from enacted regulation.

items.headline: Sample: rupee weakens against the dollar on importer demand
items.why: A weaker rupee helps exporters' reported revenue and raises import costs.
items.explanation: Demo explanation: currency moves of this size are usually background context, not an event on their own.

items.headline: Sample: monsoon season ends with rainfall near the long-period average
items.why: A normal monsoon supports rural incomes and demand for consumer goods and two-wheelers.
items.explanation: Demo explanation: slow-moving seasonal information has little short-term price effect and would score low on novelty.
